View image in fullscreen
Residents sit at a viewing platform overlooking the newly opened New Yalu River Bridge Photograph: Florence Lo/Reuters
North Korea has opened up bridges to Russia and China – in which direction will it go?
Kim Jong-un has opened the borders to both his key allies in Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, but for different reasons
For more than a decade, local Chinese residents pilloried it as nothing more than an empty bridge that led to a North Korean vegetable patch on the other side.
Fast forward 12 years and dozens of trucks are now traversing the bridge linking China to North Korea, boosting trade for the reclusive regime. But it has also triggered concern that it could intensify a struggle for influence over the North between Beijing and the region’s other major power, Russia.map
The New Yalu River Bridge connects the north-eastern Chinese city of Dandong with Sinuiju in North Korea and has four lanes and stretches 3km (1.9 miles) across the Yalu river. It is expected to ease congestion on the ageing Friendship Bridge nearby.
It opened on 15 October, about a month after another major crossing – this time between North Korea and Russia. The first road bridge across their short shared border, named the Yakov Novichenko Bridge, reportedly made Chinese officials uneasy, coming on top of signs from the North Korean leader Kim Jong-un that he is prioritising ties with Moscow.map
“China’s interest in buttressing its influence in North Korea is certainly reinforced by the diversifying North Korea-Russia relationship — ties that China tolerates but watches closely as they add complexity to its relationship with its provocative neighbour,” says Carla Freeman, director of the Johns Hopkins School of Advanced International Studies’ Foreign Policy Institute.

item.title: [CBS News World] Deadly shooting in Paris suburb investigated as terrorism, officials say
item.description:
A gunman shooting from his car killed one person and wounded several others in the Paris suburb of Trappes on Friday, in what authorities described as a racially motivated act of terrorism.
President Emmanuel Macron called it "a racist terror attack" and said the suspect's statements suggested it was premeditated.
The alleged shooter was "firing at random, wanting to cause a bloodbath" as he drove through Trappes and neighboring La Verriere, Trappes mayor Ali Rabeh told broadcaster BFMTV.
"This is probably one of the first attempted mass killings motivated by Islamophobia and racism," Rabeh told reporters, The Associated Press reported. "This was a terrorist attack with racist, likely Islamophobic, overtones."
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said the suspect fired "what appears to have been a military-grade weapon, or at least an automatic weapon." Rabeh called it a "miracle" that there were not more casualties.
Rabeh said that the gunman targeted passersby at three separate locations, including a playground. Forensic investigators were also seen examining evidence at a gas station.
The alleged shooter was arrested in the nearby town of Coignieres. Nuñez said the attack lasted just under 15 minutes and was stopped by five officers from the anti-crime brigade.

Dimitar DILKOFF /AFP via Getty Images
Officials initially said four people had been wounded, but Rabeh told reporters there were five, including three who were very seriously injured, with their lives in danger.

Stephen Hubbard (second from left in the first row) was flown back home on a US plane earlier this weekByDan JohnsonUkraine correspondent in KyivPublished5 hours ago
Ukrainians held alongside freed US prisoner Stephen Hubbard have said they witnessed him being beaten and humiliated by Russian guards during his four-year detention.
Dmytro Khyliuk first met Hubbard at the Novozybkov prison in Bryansk, not far from Russia's border with Ukraine, in September 2022.
"We heard it from the guards. They came during inspections and were asking: in which cell is the American? And then they used obscene words. They threatened him, they mocked him from the first days."
Ihor Shyshko also remembers Hubbard's arrival at the jail and says his nationality marked him out to the officers.
"It attracted such attention because they mocked him, forced him to learn the Russian language, sing the national anthem and repeat the rules of the prison schedule, which he could not read."
Hubbard was captured in April 2022, when Russian soldiers occupied the eastern city of Izyum, where he was living with his Ukrainian partner.
He was accused of serving in Ukraine's armed forces and convicted in a trial in Moscow before being sentenced to six years and 10 months. Shyshko and Khyliuk were held alongside Hubbard as he awaited trial.

Ihor Shyshko alleges that Hubbard was subjected to sexual humiliation and abuse for the entertainment of Russian prison staff

Watch: CCTV footage appears to show gunmen near churchByJamie Whitehead and Jacob PhillipsPublished23 October 2026
Seven people have been killed in an attack on a funeral in central Jordan, officials have said.
At least 34 others were injured as gunmen opened fire on a church in Hmoud, in the Karak governorate on Friday.
The unidentified gunmen are reported to have arrived in a car, entered the church and opened fire before fleeing. No-one has admitted carrying out the attack.
In a news conference, Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya said authorities were working to apprehend the perpetrators which he described as a "group of extremists".
Jordan's King Abdullah II said authorities would "confront the terrorist act that targeted Karak with the harshest penalties".
Initial reports indicated seven people had been killed in the attack. A government spokesperson later said six people had died, before officials again revised the death toll to seven.
CCTV footage, verified by the BBC, appears to shows three gunmen making their way from a road toward the church.
Two of the attackers are seen making their way on to what appears to be a vehicle entrance to the church grounds, before retreating briefly and returning with a third man. All three appear to be armed with handguns.
Separate footage believed to be from the aftermath of the attack appears to show several dead and wounded bodies on the ground amid chaotic scenes.
Image source, ReutersImage caption,
Between 150 and 200 people were in the church at the time of the shooting, according to one witness
Witnesses have described scenes of panic inside the church as people threw themselves under pews searching for cover, moving away from the windows.
Prayers and screams could be heard throughout the building as some tried to flee.

item.description:

Watch: Emergency services at the scene of shooting near ParisByPaul Kirby, Europe digital editor and Jacob PhillipsPublished23 October 2026
French President Emmanuel Macron has labelled a gun attack in a Parisian suburb which killed one person and injured five others "a racist terrorist attack".
Macron said the attack was a "turning point in the life of our Republic and our nation" - the first time there has ever been a random racial killing like this.
The attack unfolded over some 15 minutes with the attacker opening fire from his car - first in Trappes to the south-west of Paris, and then in nearby La Verrière - appearing to target people of migrant origin. He was subsequently arrested.
Three of those injured, including a 12-year-old girl, remain in a serious condition.
Visiting the scene of the attack in Trappes, Macron said people had been targeted for their skin colour or religion and urged the public not to give an inch in the face of what he called "ideologies taking root".
The exact motive remains unclear, but the National Anti-Terrorist Prosecutor's Office (PNAT) said the incident appeared to be "murder in connection with a terrorist enterprise".
The suspect has been named in French media as Kevin T who, according to PNAT, had four previous convictions which had been "automatically expunged".
The 39-year-old was known to police but not to France's intelligence services, local media report.
He was not on a list of individuals considered to be a serious threat to French security, the national anti-terrorism prosecutor's office told BFMTV.
A member of the suspect's "immediate family circle" was also taken into custody on Friday, it added.
The Mayor of Trappes, Ali Rabeh, said that "an individual fired shots from his vehicle at several people he encountered" on Friday morning.

item.title: [ABC News World] Part of famous Brighton pier collapses as Atlantic storms sweep into England
item.description:
Part of famous Brighton pier collapses as Atlantic storms sweep into England
Part of the ruins of one of England’s most recognizable piers has collapsed into the seaByPAN PYLAS Associated PressOctober 23, 2026, 5:03 AM
LONDON -- Part of the ruins of one of England's most recognizable piers partially collapsed into the sea on Friday as the first of this weekend's two major storms swept in from the Atlantic, knocking out power to thousands of homes and businesses.
A section of the remnants of the historic West Pier in the popular southern England town of Brighton fell into the sea as it was buffeted by tall waves pushed by a storm the U.K.'s national forecaster has named Austen.
It's the latest diminution of the structure, which was set ablaze in 2003.
“Ever since the two devastating arson attacks in 2003, the West Pier has been whittled away by nature," said Professor Fred Grey, an honorary historian at the West Pier Trust. "All ruins are alive and ever-changing, and this is true of the West Pier.”
The Met Office issued an amber warning — the second highest — for wind gusts of up to 80 mph (130 kph) in Cornwall and Devon as Storm Austen blows eastward along the English Channel coast. And forecasters on Jersey issued a red warning for shipping around the Channel Islands, where gusts of up to 80 mph also were expected.
According to the National Grid electricity distributor, more than 31,000 homes were without power in the southwest by mid-afternoon. Engineers had restored power to more than 52,000 properties since Storm Austen began.

Mystery over source of Ebola infection in Nigeria fuels concern about spread of virus
Switzerland says patient is wife of Swiss diplomat and believed to have contracted virus while travelling in Uganda
Health officials across Africa are racing to determine how Nigeria’s first Ebola patient ⁠in more than a decade ⁠became infected, amid fears ​the outbreak could spread further after reaching a fourth African country.
The Swiss foreign ministry said on Friday the patient in Nigeria, the Ugandan-born wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja, had not travelled to the Democratic Republic of ⁠Congo, where the outbreak was first detected in mid-May before spreading to Uganda, Kenya and now Nigeria. The woman was believed to have contracted Ebola while travelling with her husband in Uganda, the ministry added.
The new information contradicts accounts from Uganda, which previously said the woman had travelled to eastern DR Congo, and will raise concerns about the ability of authorities to contain the outbreak, which is already the most geographically widespread in history.
The Ugandan government reported Ebola cases in May and June before WHO declared it Ebola-free in August. A Ugandan government spokesperson told Reuters on Thursday that Uganda had no ​Ebola cases and that, if ​it did, it would make that information ​public.
The World Health Organization said investigations were continuing to establish the likely source of infection for the Ebola patient in Nigeria.

item.title: [ABC News World] Philippines announce bounty on senator wanted by the ICC
item.description:
Philippines announce bounty on senator wanted by the ICC
Philippine officials announce a bounty for the capture of Senator Ronald dela Rosa, who faces arrest by the International Criminal Court for alleged crimes against humanityByJIM GOMEZ Associated PressOctober 23, 2026, 6:40 AM
Share
MANILA, Philippines -- Philippine officials announced a bounty Friday for the capture of a senator who has been ordered arrested by the International Criminal Court for an alleged crime against humanity in connection with deadly anti-drugs crackdowns.
The court alleges that Sen. Ronald dela Rosa, 64, was an “indirect co-conspirator” of former President Rodrigo Duterte, who was arrested last year and now faces trial for alleged crimes linked to the so-called war on drugs he waged while in office.
Dela Rosa last appeared in public when he went to the Philippine Senate briefly in May but fled after the international court in The Hague, Netherlands, made public a warrant for his arrest.
Dela Rosa was the first national police chief designated by Duterte to enforce the brutal crackdowns he launched after becoming president in 2016. After dela Rosa retired from the police force, he was appointed as a top prisons official before successfully running for a Senate seat in 2019.
Estimates of the death toll in the crackdown on drugs during Duterte’s presidential term vary, from the more than 6,000 reported by the national police to up to 30,000 claimed by human rights groups.
Duterte and dela Rosa denied authorizing extrajudicial killings.
The ICC warrant, originally issued confidentially in November last year, charged dela Rosa with murder of “no less than 32 persons” allegedly committed between July 2016 and April 2018.

item.title: [ABC News World] Pope Leo XIV cancels Assisi trip on doctors' advice as he recovers from surgery
item.description:
Pope Leo XIV cancels Assisi trip on doctors' advice as he recovers from surgery
Pope Leo XIV will not travel to Assisi on Tuesday for a major interfaith peace gathering because he is continuing to recover from thoracic surgery he underwent last week, the Vatican said FridayByThe Associated PressOctober 23, 2026, 4:01 AM
Share
VATICAN CITY -- VATICAN CITY (AP) — Pope Leo XIV will miss a planned trip to Assisi next week on doctors’ orders as he continues recovering from thoracic surgery he underwent last Tuesday, the Vatican said Friday.
The pope had been due to attend an Oct. 27 gathering marking the 40th anniversary of St. John Paul II’s World Day of Prayer for Peace.
In a statement, the Vatican said Leo was advised not to travel “to facilitate his recovery” from the surgery. The pope will instead send a message to organizers, Christian and other religious leaders, and guests attending the event, titled “Disarmed and Disarming Peace.”
The Vatican said Leo wanted to express his closeness to participants and reaffirm his belief that the “spirit of Assisi,” dialogue and the search for words and gestures of peace remain valuable resources at a time of conflict.
The Assisi meeting commemorates the landmark interfaith peace gathering convened by St. John Paul II in 1986.

Severe flooding in eastern Spain and UK hit by first named storm of winter Megan Davies, Claire Jones and Magdalena Shopova for MetDesk
Storm Adam brings torrential rain to Valencia, Alicante and Balearic Islands, as Storm Austen strikes England and Wales
Storm Adam brought torrential rain to eastern Spain earlier this week. In Pego, Alicante, 632mm fell in 36 hours, with 430mm of this falling in just six hours, while the Valencian town of Olivia received 600mm in 24 hours.
The severe flooding led 145 municipalities across Valencia and Alicante to impose a temporary lockdown on about 850,000 people on Monday. At least five people have died, 500 have been rescued and 2,100 evacuated.
The storm also affected the Balearic Islands, with more than 130 incidents recorded in Ibiza including standing water at the airport causing some flights to be diverted or suspended. Although the worst of the storm has passed and conditions are improving across Valencia and Alicante, local disruption is expected to continue.
The first named storm of the winter for the UK is tracking through the Channel. Storm Austen is bringing damaging winds not only to south-west England and Wales, but south-west Ireland and northern France. Gusts are expected to be around 50-60mph, but some exposed north-western coasts of France could experience winds of up to 80-90mph.

Lewis Hamilton aims to extend career till early 2030s so he can race in African Grand Prix
41-year-old set on ‘dream to be able to race in Africa’
Rwanda to host despite criticism of human rights record
Lewis Hamilton has said he hopes to remain racing in Formula One until he can take part in the African Grand Prix which is set to take place in Rwanda in the 2030s. The seven-time world champion believes it is right that F1 is to hold a race there despite criticism of the country’s human rights record.
Last week F1 confirmed Rwanda was to host the African Grand Prix having concluded a 10-year agreement for the meeting on a purpose-built circuit, with the first race set for the early 2030s. It is lined up to be held on a circuit in Bugesera, 25 miles south of the capital, Kigali, which has yet to be constructed and marks a return to the African continent for the first time since it last held a race at Kyalami, South Africa in 1993.Austin GP is about much more than potential for Antonelli’s first F1 world title | Giles Richards
Read more
Hamilton has been championing a race in Africa for some time. The 41-year-old is understood to be currently contracted with Ferrari until the end of the 2027 season, and speaking before this weekend’s US Grand Prix he said he would like to continue racing for at least another four years in order to make it to the meeting in Rwanda.
“I’m now forced to have to stay a lot longer because we have a race in Africa and that’s been my dream to be able to race in Africa,” he said. “So, I have to keep fighting to try and stay fit if I can. If I can still punch out good results over the next year, we’ll keep it going.”

item.description:
Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption,
"Purchase to sit" signs are popping up in Starbucks stores around ChinaByKoh EwePublished22 October 2026
Taking a seat at a Starbucks in China? Just make sure you're also ordering something there.
A new policy by Starbucks China takes effect across all its 8,000 stores on Thursday, making it mandatory for people to purchase items if they want to sit in its cafes.
Starbucks China said the move was part of efforts to improve the "in-store experience" for customers. The company is facing stiff competition from homegrown brands such as Luckin Coffee.
Starbucks stores around the world have also been wrestling with non-paying seat-hoggers and other undesirable behaviour from customers.
In South Korea, Starbucks has told customers to stop bringing "bulky items" into their stores, after some patrons reportedly hogged seats with printers and desktop computers in tow.
In North America, Starbucks reversed its open-door policy which for years allowed people to use their seats and toilets without buying anything, saying that it wanted to "prioritise" paying customers.
Starbucks China is now following suit.
Ahead of the official announcement on Wednesday, reports of the new seating policy at China's Starbucks stores had been circulating this week - along with social media videos of what appear to be "purchase to sit" signs in Starbucks stores.
Many on Chinese social media welcomed the new policy.
"Finally, there won't be peak periods where people are just sitting there not ordering anything, drinking Luckin coffee, playing games and yelling on the phone," reads one of the top-liked comment on Weibo. "Every time I walk around, there's nowhere to sit,"
"There's nothing wrong with it. I'd feel awkward sitting there if I didn't make a purchase. I'd rather leave the seats for those who made purchases and need the seats," another Weibo user commented.

Controversial US-backed vaccine trial in African newborns halted
Hepatitis B study in Guinea-Bissau that was to be funded by CDC and that drew global backlash ‘will not move forward’
The US-backed hepatitis B vaccine trial in African newborns that drew global backlash was halted, the lead researcher said on Wednesday.
It was “now clear” that the study “will not move forward in Guinea-Bissau”, Frederik Schaltz-Buchholzer, a Danish researcher, wrote on LinkedIn, adding, “we were not given the necessary governmental approval.”
The minister of health in Guinea-Bissau, Quinhin Nantote, previously denied that the project would move forward. “This is not even remotely true,” Nantote told the Guardian in Portuguese last week.
The study was to be funded with $1.6m from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), along with another $1.6m from private partners like the Bill Ackman-backed Pershing Square Foundation and the Bluebell Foundation.
“The solution is clear here: take the money and vaccinate as many kids as you can,” said Paul Offit, a vaccines expert at the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia, who sharply criticized the proposed study as unethical.
The government of Guinea-Bissau now has control over the researchers’ vaccines, which they apprehended when they searched the offices of the Bandim Health Project on Monday.
It was vital to support Guinea-Bissau in rolling the immunizations out to all newborns as soon as possible, Offit said. Guinea-Bissau currently plans to offer the universal birth dose in 2028.

item.description:
Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption,
China has been positioning itself as a mediator for conflicts in the Middle EastByKoh EwePublished16 October 2026
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi has told Israel to stop its "forced establishment" of settlements in the West Bank and reverse its actions, his office said.
The "Palestinian question" is "the greatest historical injustice of this century", Wang told Israeli President Isaac Herzog in a face-to-face meeting on the sidelines of a conference in Azerbaijan on Thursday.
Beijing has been a long-standing supporter of the Palestinian cause and has maintained that a "two-state solution" is the "correct direction".
It has also been positioning itself as a mediator for conflicts in the Middle East.
In 2023 Beijing brokered a deal to restore diplomatic ties between Iran and Saudi Arabia after years of hostility. Earlier this year, it was part of efforts, along with Pakistan, to propose a ceasefire in the US-Israel war against Iran.
Beijing's efforts to tackle the war in Gaza have focused on Palestinian unity.
In 2024 Beijing got rival Palestinian factions to agree to form an interim "national reconciliation government" for the occupied West Bank and Gaza after the war with Israel, although it was never implemented.
Now, Wang says the "immediate priority" is to fully open access to Gaza and stop the continued spread of a "humanitarian catastrophe".
China is willing to work with the international community to get the parties to return to dialogue and "seek a political solution to the conflict", he said.
In a post on X, Herzog said he was "pleased" to meet Wang and their talk "focused on the relations between our countries and the situation in the Middle East".
"I emphasised Israel's desire for peace in the region, alongside the strategic threats to our security, first and foremost from Iran and its terror proxies," he wrote.

item.title: [BBC China] North Korea and China open new bridge after 12-year delay
item.description:
Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption,
The New Yalu River Bridge spans 3km (1.9 miles) from the Chinese border city of Dandong to Sinuiju in North KoreaByKoh Ewe and Julianna KhanPublished15 October 2026
A long-delayed road bridge linking China and North Korea has opened, Chinese state media report, as trade ties improve between the neighbours.
China is North Korea's largest trading partner and a lifeline against heavy international sanctions over Pyongyang's nuclear weapons programme.
The New Yalu River Bridge spans 3km (1.9 miles) from the Chinese border city of Dandong to Sinuiju in North Korea, and is set to become the main land route for trade between them.
Its launch, initially slated for 2014, had been indefinitely postponed after North Korea halted construction of its roads and customs facilities, as relations with Beijing turned frosty.
Chinese Premier Li Qiang, in a video address on Thursday, said the bridge was a "new landmark symbolising the traditional friendship between China and North Korea", and that the two countries were "opening a new chapter" in bilateral ties.
The New Yalu River Bridge is an alternative to the decades-old Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge, which was built between 1937 and 1943 during Imperial Japan's occupation of the region.
The new bridge is an "important facility for connectivity" between the two countries, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Wednesday, adding that the route would "further facilitate trade and people-to-people exchanges".
Last year, bilateral trade reached $2.7bn, marking a recovery to pre-pandemic levels, mostly fuelled by Chinese exports to North Korea.
A sharp and sudden increase in trade across the border is "unlikely" as the UN sanctions on North Korea remain in effect, Kang Jun-young, a professor of Chinese studies at the Hankuk University of Foreign Studies, tells the BBC.
